---
title: "Exploring Students Mental Health"
format:
  html:
    echo: false
---
This analysis examines the complex relationships between various psychological and demographic factors affecting student mental health. Using a dataset of 27,901 Indian student records, we explore how different aspects of student life correlate with depression and other mental health indicators.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false 
#| message: false
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 8

# Load libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
data <- read.csv("data/student_depression.csv")
# Calculate stats
depression_stats <- data %>%
  group_by(Depression) %>%
  summarise(Count = n()) %>%
  mutate(Percentage = Count / sum(Count) * 100,
         Status = ifelse(Depression == 1, "Depressed", "Not Depressed"))

# Determine y-axis upper limit
y_max <- max(depression_stats$Count) * 1.15  # Add 15% padding

# Create plot with adjusted limits
ggplot(depression_stats, aes(x = Status, y = Count, fill = Status)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%d\n(%.1f%%)", Count, Percentage)), 
            vjust = -0.5, size = 4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Depressed" = "#E74C3C", "Not Depressed" = "#2ECC71")) +
  labs(title = "Depression Status Among Students",
       x = "Depression Status",
       y = "Number of Students") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, y_max))  # Set dynamic upper limit
```

This project is focused on studying the causes of depression or related factors. I believe it is very important to have a mentally healthy youth, as they are the future of our society. As can be seen in the graph above, among students, there are more people suffering from depression than healthy ones—even though this analysis only covered India, I think this situation is common everywhere. If we understand the causes and consequences, we can fight against it.
